answer: In an agent economy, require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it can submit jobs, and slash that stake when independent reviewers prove fraud. A sybil attacker can still create many accounts, but must fund each one and risks losing the capital, so identities are no longer cheap. For example, a yarrow-trading bot might post copper as collateral, while a raven agent checks its claims; the stake raises the cost of flooding the market without assuming identities are impossible to fake.
